cues.text: Every shift, you pump solvent, move pallets and slit rolls.
You know these jobs. But today, something might be different.
Before your hands move, take two minutes.
The 2-minute rule: pause at the point of work, before you start,
cues.tts: The two-minute rule: pause at the point of work, before you start,

cues.text: and after any break, handover, interruption, or change.
cues.tts: and after any break, handover, interruption, | or change.

cues.text: Two minutes is a guide. What matters is the pause.
You already do line clearance for product.
This is line clearance for people.
It adds to procedures, permits, lockout and guards. It never replaces them.
Stop. Hands off.
cues.tts: Stop. | Hands off.

cues.text: Look around the job and compare with the plan.
Ask four questions: What's different? What could hurt us?
cues.tts: Ask four questions. What's different? | What could hurt us?

cues.text: Checked or assumed? What if it goes wrong?

Checked means you saw or tested it yourself.
Assumed means you're guessing.
cues.tts: Checked means you saw or tested it yourself. Assumed means you're guessing.

cues.text: Decide: Go, Fix it, or Stop & get help. That's your call.
cues.tts: Decide: Go, | fix it, | or stop and get help. That's your call.

cues.text: Fix it only if you're trained and authorized, and it's a step in your procedure.
cues.tts: Fix it, only if you're trained and authorized, and it's a step in your procedure.

cues.text:
No permit yet? Someone else's unfinished work?
Not authorized? Stop & get help.
cues.tts: No permit yet? Someone else's unfinished work? Not authorized? Stop and get help.

cues.text: Not sure, or the fix doesn't work? Stop & get help.
cues.tts: Not sure, or the fix doesn't work? Stop and get help.

cues.text: Before you start, you'll move a laminate roll with the roll lifter.
What's different? Nothing. What could hurt us? A heavy roll.
Checked or assumed? Checked. You tested the grip.
What if it goes wrong? Nobody's in the aisle. Your call?
cues.tts: What if it goes wrong? Nobody's in the aisle. | Your call?

cues.text: Go. That took seconds.
Most pauses end in Go.
But sometimes a pause catches a problem. That's a save.
Here are four examples, not real events.
Each one asks you twice: find the problem, then pick your call.
In the mix room, before you start, you'll pump flammable solvent from a drum.
Hands off. What would make you stop here?

Checked or assumed?
The bonding clamps that stop static sparks are still on their hook.
cues.tts: Checked or assumed? The bonding clamps that stop static sparks are still on their hook.

cues.text: An unbonded drum or pump can hold a static charge and spark.
Your call?
Fix it. Bonding is a step in your procedure. Clamps first, on bare metal.
With drum and pump bonded, the lamp turns green. Go.
No static spark where the vapor comes out.
After your break, you head to roll staging for the next roll.
Look closely. What would make you stop here?
What's different? The roll's up high now. That's a forklift job.

Your card says pallet truck only.
A forklift's a different truck, with its own training.
cues.tts: Your card says pallet truck only. A forklift's a different truck, with its own training.

cues.text: A co-worker means well: “Line's waiting. Just grab the forklift!”
cues.tts: A co-worker means well: “Line's waiting. Just grab the forklift.”

cues.text: So, your call?
Stop & get help. You're not authorized to drive a forklift.
cues.tts: Stop and get help. You're not authorized to drive a forklift.

cues.text: Say it kindly: “Thanks, but I'm not trained on that one. I'll call our lead.”
Your lead sends a trained driver. You stand clear.
Then it's Go.
Nobody drives a truck they're not trained on.
At handover, the die cutter's note says it's ready to run.
Now, what would make you stop here?
Checked or assumed? The guard's off the die station, where patches are cut.
And someone else's lock is still on.
What's your call?
Stop & get help. It's someone else's unfinished work.
cues.tts: Stop and get help. It's someone else's unfinished work.

cues.text: Only the lock's owner removes it, or a supervisor, using the site's lock-removal procedure.

The owner finishes, puts the guard back and removes their lock.
You run restart checks. Go.
cues.tts: The owner finishes, puts the guard back and removes their lock. You run restart checks. Go.

cues.text: The die cutter never starts with the guard off and the work unfinished.
The slitter changes over to a potent product, strong in tiny amounts.
Your turn. What would make you stop here?

What could hurt us? This product, on bare wrists.
Now it's double gloves and sleeve covers.
cues.tts: What could hurt us? This product, on bare wrists. Now it's double gloves and sleeve covers.

cues.text: And your call?
Fix it. Putting on the right gear is your own gowning step.

Do a normal stop, step away,
and take off your gloves as your procedure says.
cues.tts: Do a normal stop, step away, and take off your gloves as your procedure says.

cues.text: Wash hands and wrists with soap and water, not hand sanitizer.
Then put on inner gloves, sleeve covers, and outer gloves over the cuffs. Go.
No small, repeated doses from a product made to pass through skin.
Two were Fix it, two were Stop & get help. All four end in Go once it's safe.
cues.tts: Two were Fix it, two were Stop and get help. All four end in Go, once it's safe.

cues.text: Most pauses end in Go, right away.
Anyone can stop a job, staff or contractor, even on a late batch. No punishment, no blame.
Leaders commit to come quickly, thank you, fix the cause and tell you what changed.
The pause isn't a form. Report what you caught the usual way.

Decide: Go, Fix it, or Stop & get help.

cues.text: When in doubt, get help. That's the 2-minute rule: line clearance for people.

cues.text: Find out who you call for help: days, nights and weekends.
